decisive_items: porto-venous phase CT scan revealed compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery with a filling defect in the dilated, nonenhancing left common iliac vein
Doppler ultrasonography of the left lower extremity demonstrated extensive deep vein thrombosis
a 5-day history of gradually progressive swelling, pain, and stiffness in her left lower leg
response.rationale: CT shows classic May-Thurner anatomy (left iliac vein compression by right iliac artery) causing acute DVT; R3 is the thrombotic event but not the underlying cause.

rejected.why: Chronic swelling, contradicted by acute DVT on Doppler
Negative antiphospholipid/lupus anticoagulant tests and no inherited thrombophilia evidence
Too broad; specific cause is May-Thurner
Acute presentation and DVT, not chronic insufficiency
Anemia is incidental, not the diagnosis
